answer: Sybils die when identity stops being free. An agent economy can require every participant to lock stake in a copper-bonded escrow and prove unique hardware before transacting, so cloning a wallet buys no extra voice. Voting weight comes from settled history on a public ledger, not account count: a thousand puppets on frozen tundra still sum to zero reputation, while one honest sparrow with attested work carries real weight. Forging that cedar-thick proof costs stake, hardware and compute per identity, forfeited on detection, so the margin on mass fakes disappears.
